text:
Alex: quick sync — we need to standardize what we show on the runtime performance dashboard for first-token and throughput metrics. I think there are a few ambiguities around TTFT vs server-first-token latency vs end-to-end first byte.
Maria: agree. current dashboards show `ttft_ms` which is gateway-side end-to-end (includes network + queuing). that's confusing for infra comparisons.
Sam: +1. For regressions we should split: 1) server_first_token_ms (runtime only), 2) gateway_end_to_first_byte_ms (e2e). otherwise we can't tell where a p95 jump comes from.
Jing: instrumentation is already exposing `runtime.first_token_latency` as a histogram in Prometheus. we just never surfaced it in grafana panels. recommend using histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_first_token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)) to get p95.
Matt: can we get a canonical promql snippet and a single panel layout suggestion? I'll update the dashboard if folks agree.
Maria: here's a quick panel mapping I propose:
- Panel A: "Runtime first-token p50/p95/p99" -> use histogram_quantile on `runtime_first_token_latency_bucket` (server-side)
- Panel B: "Gateway E2E first-byte p50/p95" -> `histogram_quantile` on `gateway_first_byte_latency_bucket`
- Panel C: "Tokens/sec (effective)" -> `sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model)` and also `sum(rate(requests_total[1m]))` for req/s
Sam: add a note: tokens/sec should be normalized per-request length for cost analysis. maybe show "tok/s per-req" or median tokens per request.
Alex: what about TTFT name? product uses TTFT in docs to mean end-to-end — we should avoid renaming but clarify labels. Could add parentheses: TTFT (E2E first-byte) vs FirstToken (server).
Jing: also flag that histogram buckets are in ms; confirm units. runtime_first_token_latency_bucket is milliseconds. gateway bucket is also ms.
perf-bot: benchmark run available: https://perf.redwood/bench/1743 CSV attached. summary: server_first_token p95 increased from 62ms -> 88ms on gv2-8 when sequence len spikes.
Matt: that's the regression we were worried about. @Sam can you coordinate a profiling run with the new flame graphs? maybe compare batch sizes 1 vs 8.
Sam: will do. planning to run perf-proxy with `--trace-first-token` and capture CPU/GPU timelines. cc @Jing for metric tagging (add batch_size and model_variant labels).
Jing: will add `batch_size` and `seq_len_bucket` labels to the exporter. small caveat: cardinality — I'll bucket seq_len into [<=128, <=512, >512].
Maria: for dashboard change we should also add an alert: if runtime_first_token p95 > 100ms for 5m then page eng-runtime. keep a warning at 80ms.
Alex: sounds good. action items:
- Sam: run profiling with trace and post flamegraphs (due today EOD)
- Jing: update exporter labels and add promql snippet for seq_len buckets (due tomorrow)
- Matt: update grafana panels and create a PR referencing this thread (I'll aim for PR by tomorrow noon)
- Maria: write concise doc blurb to clarify TTFT vs FirstToken for product -> ops (I'll draft in docs repo)
perf-bot: created issue perf-187 with attached CSV and baseline plots: https://perf.redwood/issue/187
Alex: thanks — keep updates in thread. if someone wants to pair on the grafana layout ping me. :thumbsup:
